previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes and a history of recurrent nausea and vomiting was admitted after failing to tolerate oral intake despite initial ED management. She was found to have hypokalemia and a positive urine analysis, though the culture later indicated contamination. Treatment focused on rehydration, correcting electrolytes, and managing nausea. Based on prior endoscopy showing H. pylori gastritis, she was started on a two-week course of amoxicillin and levofloxacin with omeprazole. An ultrasound showed no liver abnormalities, but further workup for esophageal varices was pending. Her mood was low during admission, prompting continued sertraline and social support. She improved, tolerated a regular diet, and was discharged home with follow-up in primary care and gastroenterology.

dependent diabetes likely complicated by gastroparesis, and with 
depression recently started on sertraline, admitted with nausea, 
vomiting, and possible though unimpressive serotonin syndrome. 
.  
# Serotonin syndrome: possible serotonin syndrome given recent 
initiation of sertraline, combined with tramadol and zofran. 
Toxicology was consulted and do not feel that she had major 
serotonin syndrome. However, they could not rule it out, given 
labile blood pressure and heart rate and noted tremulousness and 
hyperreflexia by ED staff. During admission, she was not noted 
to have any further tremulousness or hyperreflexia. Her tramadol 
and zofran were held during this admission, and should be 
avoided from now on. Sertraline was also stopped, and psychiatry 
was consulted (see below). She was otherwise treated 
symptomatically with IVF and ativan prn tremulousness, 
agitation, and dysautonomia, with good effect. Her urine and 
serum tox were negative. Sertraline can be restarted and 
uptitrated in the outpatient setting. 
.  
# sinus tachycardia: possibly ___ serotonin syndrome vs volume 
depletion from emesis and diarrhea. She remained in sinus 
tachycardia initially and was monitored on telemetry with 
otherwise no events. Her orthostatic vital signs were consistent 
with volume depletion and she was given IVF. This resolved by 
time of discharge.
.
# N/V, gastroparesis, H. pylori infection: She was treated with 
antiemetics with reglan, avoiding zofran. We continued treatment 
for H pylori (amoxicillin, levofloxacin, PPI). Upon further 
questioning, she did not take some of her H pylori treated prior 
to admission, so her course was continued to end on ___ weeks 
of therapy. She was initially made NPO but her diet was advanced 
successfully.
.
#Diabetes, DM1, uncontrolled with complications: Patient has a 
history of poorly controlled Type 1 DM. Some ketones on urine, 
although FSG not thus far not floridly out of control. AG 
borderline, no ketones in blood. Her anion was initially 
borderline. She was maintained on lantus (decreased dose while 
NPO) and HISS q6h while NPO, and IVF. Her AG normalized quickly, 
and her sugars were well controlled. She was discharged on her 
home regimen of insulin therapy.
.  
# Depressed mood: On last admission, was noted to be depressed 
for several months and emotional and tearful during admission. 
She was apparently previously started on sertraline at least in 
___, but this was d/c'd per psychiatry consult on ___ 
given possible side effects of nausea and vomiting and unclear 
diagnosis of depression. It is unclear how she was restarted on 
this, but it may have been due to a repeat admission during 
which an error in medicine reconciliation was made. Nonetheless, 
she was noted to have depressed mood during this admission, 
despite the Zoloft prescription. Psychiatry was consulted and 
confirmed that she subjectively met criteria for depression, 
although it was unclear whether her history was entirely 
believable. They thought that she may benefit from later 
restarting of Zoloft or starting Cymbalta as an outpt, despite 
possible (though minor) serotonin syndrome during this 
admission, as long as tramadol and Zofran were avoided. ___ 
service was also consulted and thought that Cymbalta would also 
significantly benefit her ___ regimen, given that it is likely 
that her ___ has a significant psychiatric component. Pt's PCP 
felt strongly that she should restart her SSRI. However, this 
was deferred to the outpatient setting giving the above. 
Appointment was made with ___ provider to follow up after 
discharge. He will arrange for patient to have a psychiatric 
appointment to consider reinitiation of SSRI. Pt instructed that 
is absolutely essential that she attend her outpatient f/u 
appointments.  
.  
# Social/Dispo: Given her multiple admissions and apparently 
uncontrolled depression, ___, and nausea and vomiting, it was 
thought to be imperative to form a multidisciplinary team 
involving her PCP, ___, psychiatry, ___, and possibly SW. SW was 
consulted during this admission to help with management. Pt has 
PCP, ___, SW and ___ follow up as an outpatient. Pt has not seen 
psych at ___ as an outpatient and she would have to call for a 
follow up. HOwever, SW at ___ has been arranged. Pt has had 
multiple appointments made with this provider but has yet to 
establish care.

# Chronic low back ___ from MVA: On admission, she appeared 
oversedated on dilaudid. She stated that she was chronically 
taking dilaudid, although this was not confirmed on discharge

were supposed to be avoided for her. She was initially treated
